description: TEMPORARY validation profile for the Meshy auto-rigged standing baby. Not production. See docs/MESHY_RIG_VALIDATION.md.
notes: The spine chain is named counter-intuitively: Spine02 is LOWEST (32% height), then Spine01 (37%), then Spine (42%) which is the TOPMOST spine bone. 'chest' therefore maps to 'Spine', not 'Spine02'.
No finger bones exist. The hands are mitten forms; itemHold* sockets attach to the hand bone directly.

The mouth is PAINTED, not modelled: this character's face is a smooth surface, so every geometric heuristic finds the NOSE, the only thing that protrudes. Deriving the socket from the frontmost vertex put a feeding bottle on the baby's eyebrow. tools/find_face_sockets.py instead decodes the base-colour texture and profiles face colour by height: hair reads brown at 81-93%, skin is pale and near-neutral, and the lips are the one saturated red band at 61-63% (r-g peaks at 108 vs ~61 for skin). The socket is the centroid of those 36 lip vertices, pushed 0.03 off the surface so a prop does not z-fight the face.

The texture analysis alone put the mouth at 62% of height; rendering it there sat the bottle on the NOSE. The socket was lowered to 58% by measuring the gap in the render and converting with the eye-to-mouth distance as a ruler, then re-rendering to confirm. The texture method got it close and the eye settled it -- which is the order LB_RIG_V1.md prescribes ('positioned once by hand').

UNITS TRAP: socketOffsets are in BONE-LOCAL space, and this rig's bones are in CENTIMETRES under an Armature node carrying a 0.01 scale. An offset expressed in the mesh's metre-ish space is therefore ~100x too small and collapses the socket onto its parent bone -- which is exactly the bug the first version of this file shipped: 'mouth' resolved to within 1 mm of 'head'. Offsets are now computed as inverseBindMatrix[bone] * targetPointInMeshSpace, which lands in the right space and also accounts for the bone's rest rotation.
runtime_character_validation asserts the mouth sits near face height and is well clear of the head bone, so this class of mistake fails loudly rather than rendering a bottle inside the skull.
